files.design/decisions/README.md:
# Local decision lifecycle

Each record owns one choice. Drafts use State: draft in drafts/. On implementation move the same file to active/, set State: live and update inbound links. Fully replaced choices move to archive/ with State: retired and a Forward link to their replacement; the replacement links back. Rejected proposals move to declined/ with State: declined and the actual rejection reason. Keep original rationale and verification gaps. Do not add foreign markers, an .agents/notes directory or an index.
files.design/decisions/drafts/json-shape.md:
# JSON top-level shape

State: draft

Choice: --json will return a top-level array of people, while default text stays as it is.

Reason: current consumers expect an array after JSON.parse. A metadata wrapper object would require caller changes, so it is not selected.

Acceptance: complete stdout parses into the two person objects as an array.

Verification gap: no external consumer has been run.

State: draft

Proposal: add --csv for spreadsheet consumers.

Alternative: retain JSON alone. CSV would add quoting, escaping and compatibility maintenance.

Verification gap: no spreadsheet integration has been tried.

files.architecture/adr/array.md:
# Array contract
Status: implemented
Decision: stdout is one JSON array because existing clients call JSON.parse on the entire output.
Alternative rejected: JSONL breaks those clients.
Evidence: two existing client tests pass; third-party consumers not surveyed.
files.architecture/adr/stream.md:
# Streaming contract
Status: implemented
Decision: emit records incrementally within one JSON array and honor writable backpressure.
Alternative rejected: serialize the entire dataset first because peak memory doubles.
Consequence: partial output on interruption is invalid JSON; retries must restart.
Evidence: local large-data test passed; slow network pipe behavior not measured.

files.services/billing/docs/requests.md:
# Charge requests
The client returns the terminal response and tries at most three times on HTTP 429. Authorization failures are terminal. Each retry currently creates a fresh idempotency key. See [retry rationale](decisions/retry-identity.md).
files.services/billing/docs/decisions/retry-id:
# Stable identity within one charge
Status: implemented
One logical charge reuses one idempotency key across all transport retries. A later separate charge gets a new key. The server deduplicates by key, so retrying with a different key can bill twice. Alternatives: payload hashing conflates legitimate repeated purchases; disabling retries makes short throttling incidents visible. Response payloads must not be logged. Unit transport simulation checked retry identity; real gateway timeout-after-accept behavior is unverified. Replaces [early proposal](rotate-key.md).
files.services/billing/docs/decisions/rotate-k:
# Rotate keys on retry
Status: superseded
Original proposal: create a new key on each retry to simplify tracing. Replaced by [stable identity](retry-identity.md) after duplicate-billing risk was recognized. Preserve this historical explanation.
files.docs/retries.md:
# Report refresh retries
This page owns report refresh jobs, not billing. A fresh correlation ID per retry is useful for report diagnostics.
files.services/reports/README.md:

files.services/import/README.md:
